title: missing keys on Keyboard Manager
author: cammaleoo
summary: Keyboard Manager does not list shifted punctuation such as !, @, #, $, %, ^/¨, and & as standalone keys on US and Brazilian ABNT layouts.
next_action: Consolidate the report into #24714 rather than starting a separate punctuation-key implementation.

confidence.rationale: The symptoms and named symbols directly match the existing virtual-key limitation and active tracker.

judgment.rationale: The report is the same virtual-key versus produced-character limitation discussed in #27292 and actively tracked for missing punctuation in #24714.
evidence: The reporter lists only symbols normally produced through Shift or layout-specific modifier combinations.
Issue #27292 documents that Keyboard Manager remaps virtual keys and therefore does not expose every produced character as a standalone key.
Issue #24714 remains open and was updated in 2026 to track missing colon, question mark, and other punctuation targets.
judgment.recommended_action: Consolidate the report into #24714 rather than starting a separate punctuation-key implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: This report should be consolidated with the active punctuation-key tracker before any distinct code change is designed.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager does not list shifted punctuation such as !, @, #, $, %, ^/¨, and & as standalone keys on US and Brazilian ABNT layouts.
known_information: The failure occurs in both Remap a key and Remap a shortcut.
The report covers Portuguese (Brazil ABNT) and US layouts.
The same missing-symbol family is already tracked in #24714.
inferences: The unavailable entries reflect Keyboard Manager's virtual-key model, not a failure unique to one physical keyboard.
issue_context.analysis: A separate fix would duplicate the active punctuation-target tracker; the useful action is to preserve the additional ABNT examples there.
initial_investigation: Read the complete live report and discussion.
Checked the current state and maintainer explanation in #27292 and the active tracker #24714.

actions.label: Consolidate with punctuation-key tracker 24714

comment.body: This report overlaps #24714, which remains open for punctuation characters such as `:`, `?`, and other shifted or layout-specific symbols that are not exposed as standalone Keyboard Manager targets. #27292 documents the same virtual-key limitation. Please consolidate the Brazilian ABNT and US examples from this report into #24714 rather than tracking a separate implementation.
